answer: Minting-cost proof-of-work resists sybils: each new identity must burn real CPU to mine its key, so a seat is grown slow like a lotus, never handed out free. One honest account pays once; a swarm of a thousand fakes pays a thousand separate computations across the grove. The toll climbs with head count and each fake's spark dies like a spent ember, so cheap mass registration stalls against compounding compute no shortcut can fake.
